component.name: tappaas-cicd
component.description: TAPPaaS module tappaas-cicd: triage of its own critical/high CVEs (#788). The mothership: runs TAPPaaS's managers, controllers and the nightly scans, reachable by SSH from the admin network only. Verified live on hrossen: libssh and libxslt are in the closure only through python3 ansible-core (ansible-pylibssh; lxml via ncclient/jxmlease), which opnsense-controller uses for module-spec validation only (controller DESIGN.md), never to open an SSH connection or run XSLT. curl's HTTP/3 is ngtcp2's own QUIC stack, OpenSSL only for its crypto; nothing on the VM uses OpenSSL's QUIC or DTLS. perl 5.42.0 is NixOS's own scripts plus git's perl helpers.

analysis.detail: Packet-buffer retention in OpenSSL's own QUIC stack; nothing on the mothership uses it (curl's HTTP/3 runs on ngtcp2, with OpenSSL only for crypto).
NEW_CONNECTION_ID flood against OpenSSL's own QUIC stack; nothing on the mothership uses it (curl's HTTP/3 runs on ngtcp2).
DTLS handshake retransmission; nothing on the mothership speaks DTLS.
Needs a TLS server that swaps SSL_CTX mid-handshake between contexts with different providers loaded; nothing on the mothership is configured that way.
Channel callbacks after close in an SSH session; libssh is only ansible-pylibssh's, and ansible-core is used for module-spec validation, never to connect.
A libssh SSH server with GSSAPIKeyExchange; the mothership runs no libssh server (sshd is OpenSSH).
XSLT key() processing; libxslt is only lxml's, pulled in by ansible-core's validation-only dependencies, and no TAPPaaS code runs XSLT.
Compress::Raw::Zlib's vendored zlib; perl on the mothership runs NixOS's own scripts and git's helpers, none of which inflate attacker data through it.
